interest: 1932 U.S. reporting frames Japanese ultranationalism as 'fascism'.
overview: Docket for 894.00F (1932) listing five papers on fascism in Japan, including Inukai's assassination and the Kokumin Domei.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Japan

people.name: Laurence E. Salisbury
people.role: Officer, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, U.S. Department of State

subfiles.about: A despatch reporting that communism and fascism represent dangerous undercurrents in Japan aimed at destroying parliamentary government and capitalism.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Neville's despatch No. 561 warning that communism and fascism threaten parliamentary government in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 561 from Neville on Communism and Fascism in Japan

subfiles.about: A despatch analyzing Japanese reactionary societies and their disavowal of the term 'fascism' despite its ideological applicability.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Neville's despatch No. 588: Japanese reactionary societies reject the 'fascism' label, though it may fit.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 588 from Neville on Reactionary Societies and Fascism

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting press accounts linking the assassination of Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi to the fascist movement.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Johnson's telegram No. 548: newspapers blame the fascist movement for Inukai's assassination.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 548 from Johnson on the Assassination of Inukai

subfiles.about: A periodic report noting the marked increase in Japanese press coverage and discussions of fascism during May 1932.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Neville's report No. 634 on rising press use of 'fascism' in May 1932.
subfiles.title: Periodic Report No. 634 from Neville on Fascism in the Japanese Press

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum assessing the newly formed Kokumin Domei party and its reported fascist parliamentary tendencies.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Salisbury's memo calling the Kokumin Domei Japan's first fascist parliamentary party.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Salisbury on the Kokumin Domei Party
